title: 2026-03-18 Contract variance decisionworkshop and egress policy review
summary: Redwood and Nimbus reviewed proposed contract variances focused on DPA language, SLA credits, and egress fee exposure for cross-region traffic. Nimbus asked for clarity on private deployment pricing and KMS options. Redwood committed to sending a redline-friendly MSA template, running an egress/cost projection, and delivering a short technical benchmark plan.
action_items: Liam Chen (Redwood) - Share redline-friendly MSA with clause index and rationale (due: 2026-03-22)
Priya Nair (Redwood SE) - Prepare benchmark plan and sample prompt set for private deployment run (due: 2026-03-27)
Devon Kumar (Nimbus) - Provide monthly token volume estimates and expected cross-region egress patterns (due: 2026-03-25)
Elena Rossi (Nimbus) - Flag any DPA clause they cannot accept and send annotated PDF (due: 2026-03-24)
next_steps: Redwood to email MSA + DPA guidance and pricing scenarios
Schedule 60-min technical benchmark w/ Nimbus cloud ops (suggested week of 3/30)
Legal teams to exchange redlines; follow-up commercial call after redline review
header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 15:00 PDT
End: 15:52 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Marco Ruiz (Redwood Solutions); Zoe Park (Redwood CSM); Aria Patel (Nimbus Procurement); Devon Kumar (Nimbus Security); Elena Rossi (Nimbus Legal); Samir Khan (Nimbus Cloud Ops)
transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, uh, thanks for making time. This is Liam from Redwood — I'll kick us off.
[00:10] Aria Patel: Yeah thanks Liam, and hi all. We're on a pretty tight procurement window so wanted to focus the hour on the MSA/DPA variances and any egress exposures.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Great; I'll take the tech bits when they come up — quick note, Marco is here for the KMS questions.
[00:30] Elena Rossi: From legal, we have a couple non-starters in section 7.2 of the DPA, specifically the subprocessor subprocesser listing, um, and also the audit cadence.
[00:42] Liam Chen: Okay noted. In our experience we can offer a clause that supports periodic audits with a scoped SOC-2 report plus additional audit rights subject to NDA, is that — is that closer to what you need?
[00:53] Elena Rossi: Possibly. We need something that doesn't require on-site every quarter, we can't commit that. Also we want contractual clarity on data residency and deletion timelines.
[01:06] Devon Kumar: And on the security front, we need to understand key custody — can you support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS/HSM? And if yes, what are the failure modes — like if the key is revoked accidentally, what's recovery?
[01:23] Marco Ruiz: We support KMS integrations in Private mode; with Redwood Private you can bring your own key via standard KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) or an HSM. Recovery is customer-controlled — Redwood does not have access to the plaintext keys. There is a documented key rotation and recovery process; we can share the runbook.
[01:40] Samir Khan: Sorry, just to check — you're saying Private only? What about Dedicated? We have a mix of both in the footprint.
[01:47] Priya Nair: Good question. Dedicated supports customer key management in some configurations but with caveats around shared infrastructure and key escrow — it's more straightforward with Private (VPC / on-prem). We'll put the exact matrix in the follow-up.
[02:02] Aria Patel: Egress is the other big thing for procurement — our finance team flagged potential cross-region egress fees. We route some traffic between EU and US and want to avoid surprise costs.
[02:15] Liam Chen: Right; egress fees depend on deployment topology. If you keep model serving in-region, cross-region egress is minimal. For cross-region requests we can show estimated costs. Also we have options like request routing that localize inference to the nearest region to reduce charges.
[02:30] Devon Kumar: Can you do per-request routing automatically? Or is that manual?
[02:34] Priya Nair: It's policy-driven — you can set routing by latency vs cost. We'll share a sample routing policy.
[02:40] Elena Rossi: Back to SLAs — your standard SLA mentions 99.9 uptime with credits; procurement wants to understand the credit math and whether there are meaningful remedies beyond credits.
[02:51] Liam Chen: Our standard is 99.9 with service credits up to a percentage of monthly fees; enterprise customers often negotiate higher SLOs or a limited termination right for sustained misses. For Nimbus, given the expected spend, we can discuss a tailored SLA.
[03:05] Aria Patel: How long is typical negotiation on SLA variants? Our legal window is two weeks.
[03:10] Liam Chen: Two weeks is tight but workable if legal teams exchange redlines quickly. We'll aim to get a redline-friendly MSA over by Monday which should speed up the back-and-forth.
[03:19] Samir Khan: For the billing path — do you charge separately for egress vs tokens? Or is it bundled? Our last vendor billed egress separately and it killed the budget.
[03:29] Marco Ruiz: Redwood bills token usage separately; egress for model traffic may be invoiced as a separate line item depending on whether traffic leaves the region. We'll provide modeled scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[03:38] Aria Patel: Please do that — finance will want a worst-case and expected case.
[03:42] Devon Kumar: On compliance, do you provide logs and audit trails that show who accessed what keys and when? We need to feed SIEM.
[03:50] Marco Ruiz: Yes, audit logs are available; for Private deployments we can extend retention and integrate with your SIEM. For Hosted we provide token-level logs with obfuscation as needed.
[04:02] Elena Rossi: Also, we saw a clause about subprocessing that lists partners. We need the right to veto new subprocessors for certain data classes.
[04:10] Liam Chen: We try to keep that to a notification plus opt-out for high-risk categories. Full vetos are rare but can be scoped in the DPA for regulated data.
[04:21] Aria Patel: If possible, we want to limit the right to a defined set of subprocessors and a 60-day notice before adding new ones.
[04:28] Liam Chen: Noted — we'll propose language for a 60-day notice and a high-risk veto carveout.
[04:34] Priya Nair: Quick tech note — for benchmarking, what's most useful is a representative prompt set and your SLO targets, e.g., p95 latency under 300ms at X TPS. If you give us that, we can run an on-prem/private sim and share the results.
[04:49] Samir Khan: We can do that. Our initial target is p95 < 500ms for short prompts, and sustained 30 TPS for scoring workloads.
[04:58] Priya Nair: Okay that's clear. We'll map that against model families and sizing recommendations.
[05:03] Elena Rossi: One more from legal — indemnity and limitation caps. We usually see a reciprocal cap at the greater of fees paid in 12 months. Can you accept that?
[05:13] Liam Chen: Our standard limit is one year of fees for direct damages, but we can be flexible on cyber/exclusions for enterprise plans; we'll surface options in the MSA.
[05:23] Aria Patel: Great. Time check — we have about 25 minutes left, should we do a quick run through of the procurement timeline?
[05:29] Liam Chen: Yes please.
[05:31] Aria Patel: We need procurement sign-off by 4/15. Legal wants to lock DPA by end of March ideally. Finance needs modeled pricing by next Friday. Technical acceptance — we plan a two-week pilot starting early April if legal and finance commit.
[05:45] Liam Chen: Sounds doable. We'll aim to hit those gates: MSA/DPA redline to you by 3/22, pricing scenarios by 3/20, benchmark schedule for week of 3/30.
[05:56] Priya Nair: I'll also prepare a short tech checklist for the pilot: key provisioning, sample prompt set, telemetry hooks, and rollback plan.
[06:06] Devon Kumar: Do you have a standard data deletion SLA? We need proof points for regulatory audits.
[06:12] Marco Ruiz: Yes, 30 days for retention by default after request, with expedited deletion options in Private. We'll include the exact deletion flow in the follow-up doc.
[06:22] Elena Rossi: One last question: export controls / data transfers — does Redwood support Standard Contractual Clauses for EU transfers?
[06:29] Liam Chen: Yes, we support SCCs and can include them as addenda. For Private deployments within the EU region, that risk is minimized.
[06:37] Aria Patel: Okay, thanks. Anything else from Redwood?
[06:41] Zoe Park: From CSM perspective we'll coordinate the pilot onboarding checklist and resource assignment once dates are locked.
[06:48] Liam Chen: Alright — to wrap, we'll send the MSA draft, benchmark plan, and a pricing model. Expect an email with attachments and a suggested time for the technical benchmark.
[06:59] Aria Patel: Thanks all; we'll get our redlines and volume numbers back quickly.
[07:04] Liam Chen: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[07:07] [call ends]
notes: Redwood to avoid 'all or nothing' veto language; propose scoped veto for regulated data classes.
Nimbus to supply monthly volume and inter-region traffic matrix for accurate egress modeling.
Priority: legal DPA redlines by 2026-03-24 to keep procurement timeline on track.
